issue_paraphrase: The box-extraction utility that turns segmentation masks into bounding boxes crashes when a mask contains no foreground pixels at all: it tries to take the minimum and maximum over an empty set of pixel coordinates and raises a reduction error, instead of emitting a degenerate all-zero box. Users with batches that include at least one fully background mask get an exception, and the workaround is to special-case empty masks by hand. After the correction, empty masks yield [0,0,0,0] boxes and batches mixing empty and non-empty masks work normally.
fix_summary: In torchvision/ops/boxes.py::masks_to_boxes, wrap the per-mask min/max assignments in `if x.numel() > 0:` so all-zero masks keep the pre-initialized [0,0,0,0] box instead of calling torch.min/torch.max on empty tensors. Adds the doc note about empty masks and two regression tests.
notes: Self-contained, no network, no GPU. Reproducer is ~0.1s. masks_to_boxes loops per mask (slow for huge batches, fine for repro). The whole-suite golden pytest is NOT runnable against a bare era wheel: repo test files from Jan-Apr 2026 (common_utils.py etc.) import cvcuda-era helpers that released wheels strip; use the direct repro above or build torchvision from source at the commit. base version: fix merged 2026-02-01, first release containing it is 0.26.0; 0.25.0 wheel still contains the bug. In the venv, torch pulls fsspec/jinja2/networkx/sympy as prebuilt PyPI wheels (never cloned or vendored); none of the forbidden-list repositories are cloned by any part of this setup.

issue_paraphrase: Converting integer-typed bounding boxes from center/width/height form to the (x1,y1,x2,y2) corner form produces an invalid box whose top edge is negative when the box height is odd: the conversion code rounds the half-size with integer floor division so the center moves up by one extra pixel, yielding a y1 smaller than zero even though the box lies inside the image. The same conversion on float boxes (or through the ops module) is correct, so the discrepancy is visible to users who keep boxes in integer dtype. After the correction, integer conversions match the floating-point semantics and never emit negative corner coordinates.
fix_summary: torchvision/transforms/v2/functional/_meta.py::_cxcywh_to_xyxy now upcasts integer input to float, computes half = w/2 h/2 with true division, does the x1=cx-half / x2=x1+w arithmetic in float, and truncates back to the original dtype (inplace supported). Comment says it now matches torchvision.ops._box_convert._box_cxcywh_to_xyxy. Adds the non-regression test referencing issue 8887.
notes: Self-contained, no network, no GPU, ~0.1s. The subtle part is that the fix must reproduce the exact truncation semantics of the ops module (truncate toward zero on the final cast), so an agent must reason about rounding, not just clamp negatives. The golden pytest for this era suffers the same cvcuda-era import caveat as the other Jan-Apr 2026 fixes -- use the direct repro or a full source build. The issue number (#8887) is cited in the regression test comment; hidden issue numbers also appear there, so keep them out of any instruction text.

issue_paraphrase: The JPEG re-compression data transform blows up with a shape/stride error as soon as the input batch is not memory-contiguous, which happens trivially after a transpose of a video or multi-image tensor: internally it flattens the leading dimensions with a strict view that rejects any non-trivial stride pattern. Contiguous tensors of the same shape work fine, so the failure is confusing. After the correction, non-contiguous batches are accepted and produce exactly the same pixels as their contiguous copy.
fix_summary: One line in torchvision/transforms/v2/functional/_augment.py::jpeg_image: change `image.view((-1,) + image.shape[-3:])` to `image.reshape(...)` so non-contiguous leading dimensions are copied instead of rejected. Adds a regression test that transposes a 5-D uint8 batch and asserts the JPEG output equals the contiguous run.
notes: No network, no GPU. The fix is one line; the repro exercises the real compiled JPEG encoder/decoder (CPU wheel bundles libjpeg). torchvision 0.29 deprecates the image encoders (DeprecationWarning per call, harmless; suppress with -W ignore or pin exact 0.29.0). The other candidate modules in this era import cvcuda-era helpers that released wheels strip; _augment.py does not, so only that one file needs overlaying. torch 2.14 pulls fsspec etc. as PyPI wheels; no forbidden-list repository is cloned or vendored.

import torch
from torchvision import tv_tensors
from torchvision.transforms.v2 import functional as F
H, W = 64, 76
bbox = torch.tensor([[0.0, 0.0, float(W), float(H)]])   # box exactly covering the canvas
disp = torch.zeros((1, H, W, 2))                          # identity-displacement grid
out = F.elastic_bounding_boxes(bbox, format=tv_tensors.BoundingBoxFormat.XYXY, canvas_size=(H, W), displacement=disp)
assert out.shape == bbox.shape and not torch.isnan(out).any()
print('OK')

issue_paraphrase: The elastic-distortion transform crashes with an index-out-of-bounds error when it is applied to bounding boxes that span the full image: the corner coordinates of a full-canvas box land exactly on the last grid cell index, and the displacement lookup doesn't guard against that, so the kernel raises instead of warping the box. Boxes slightly smaller than the canvas work, which makes the failure look arbitrary. After the correction, corner indices are clamped to the grid bounds and full-size boxes are handled like any other.
fix_summary: torchvision/transforms/v2/functional/_geometry.py::elastic_bounding_boxes clamps the long/integer point coordinates with `index_x.clamp(0, inv_grid.shape[2] - 1)` and `index_y.clamp(0, inv_grid.shape[1] - 1)` before indexing inv_grid. Adds a regression test using a XYXY bbox equal to the canvas size.
notes: Self-contained, no network, no GPU, <1s. The failing path is reached with any displacement (even zeros) as long as a box touches the canvas boundary, so the repro is deterministic. Same cvcuda-era overlay caveat as the other Jan-Apr 2026 fixes (must also overlay functional/_utils.py). The underlying issue number (9394) is quoted in the regression test comment; keep it out of instruction text.
